name: Alpine A110 1800 (works rally car)
hook: The first event of the first World Rally Championship was won by a co-driver who entered under a nickname, and she was the first woman to win one.
story:
Picture a mountain road above Monaco in January 1973. Yellow headlamps sweep across the snowbanks. Down through the hairpins comes a small blue coupe, light enough that it seems to skip over the ice rather than grip it.

Two people are inside. Jean-Claude Andruet is driving. Beside him sits Michele Espinosi-Petit. She does not use that name on a rally entry. She signs on as "Biche" — the doe. She had been reading roads aloud for Andruet for years, one pace note at a time.

This was the Monte Carlo Rally, and it was round one of a brand-new World Rally Championship. Nobody had ever won one of these before. Alpine took the first three places, and five of the top six. The winning margin was twenty-six seconds.

So Biche became the first co-driver ever to win a world championship rally. She was also the first woman to do it. Both are still true.
description: The A110 was a small rear-engined coupe built by Alpine at Dieppe, in Normandy, until production in France ended in 1977. A fibreglass shell sat on a steel backbone chassis over Renault running gear. The works rally cars of the early 1970s carried a 1,796 cc four behind the rear axle and five gears. Alpine-Renault won the first World Rally Championship for makes in 1973. Thousands more A110s were built under licence in Spain, Mexico, Brazil and Bulgaria.
